blocking_findings: Deadline enforcement is unspecified: getaddrinfo has no per-call timeout and no enforcement mechanism is selected, so the 5000 ms requirement is unenforceable as written.

DNS rebinding/TOCTOU window is not mitigated: the original hostname is passed to P2 TLS but the selected address may be attacker-controlled at connect time with no pinning or re-validation against the allowlist.

Platform-dependent resolver ordering combined with FIRST_UNIQUE_IN_RESOLVER_ORDER_V1 and no failover means a single poisoned or unstable platform response permanently breaks the request with no recovery path.
No code or test execution exists; 6 positive and 24 negative offline case designs are unverified and cannot demonstrate that error closure, DoS limits, or continuity actually hold in practice.
required_changes: Select and specify a concrete deadline enforcement mechanism for getaddrinfo (e.g., thread cancellation, subprocess with timeout, or async resolver) and document its failure mode.
Add a post-resolution allowlist re-check binding the selected address to the original hostname at P1 connect time to close the DNS rebinding/TOCTOU gap.
Define explicit behavior when platform resolver order is unstable or returns only unusable results within the deadline, including a deterministic error path.
Convert offline case designs into executable tests and run them to validate error closure, DoS limits, handle continuity, and TLS identity preservation.
response.reason: Deadline enforcement is unenforceable as specified, DNS rebinding/TOCTOU is unmitigated, platform ordering risk has no recovery, and no executable tests exist to validate the design.
